headline: Approved Constellations contracts for ABA programs, including $1,150,436.00 and $2,399,698.00 for 2026-27.
summary: Approved contracts for special education programs, psychologists, therapy services, and curriculum. Also approved a 2026-27 communication plan, a June transfer report, and personnel recommendations. The chief operating officer was authorized to contract with additional staffing agencies after August 1, 2026, if needed, to fill 14.5 open special education positions.

decision_evidence.quote: Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Raymond, to approve the Consent Agenda. Motion passes 9-0.
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the five-year rewards agreements with BSN Sports and Under Armor. Motion passes 9-0.

Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to authorize Chief Operating Officer to contract with additional qualified staffing agencies, if necessary, after August 1, 2026, to fill remaining special education teacher vacancies for 2026-27 school year, with updates on any resulting contracts provided to the BOE. BOARD OF EDUCATION 
MONDAY, JULY 20, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Board of Education was held at NHS North on Monday, July 20, 2026.  Ms. Bishop called 
the meeting to order at 6:10 pm and asked Ms. Raymond to read the opening statement and Mr. Salvi to lead 
the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Present: Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Raymond, Ms. Lewis, Mr. Salvi, Ms. Lamphier,  
Ms. Lopez, Ms. Bishop 
 
Also Present:  Dr. Andrade, Dr. Scarpati, Ms. De Gray, Dr. Vincente, Mr. Beer, and Mr. Dionne 
Also Present:  Members of the Public, Channel 99 Videographer 
 Student Representatives Alia Saad (North)  
 
CONSENT AGENDA 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Raymond, to approve the Consent Agenda.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT AGENDA 
 
COMMUNICATIONS OUTSIDE THE CONSENT AGENDA 
 
PUBLIC QUESTION/COMMENT PERIOD LIMITED TO ITEMS ON THIS AGENDA 
 
SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Dr. Andrade provides an update on summer programs, noting 208 students in the Nashua Lifelong 
Learning Program, 40 in pre-K, 140 in ELL, 250 in Special Education Extended School Year (ESY), 
and 278 in Power Scholars. 
• He thanks teachers, support staff, administrators, and community partners for their efforts. 
• Dr. Andrade reminds families about fall athletic registration and the upcoming start of the new school 
year. 
 
BOARD RESPONSE TO SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Board members thank Dr. Andrade for the update and encourage staff to enjoy the rest of summer. 
 
STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE COMMENTS 
Ms. Saad tells everyone to enjoy summer. 
 
COMMITTEE ON BUDGET 
 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND OPERATIONS 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the five-year rewards agreements with BSN Sports 
and Under Armor.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the purchase of SIPPS Literacy Curriculum from 
Collaborative Classroom at a cost not to exceed $43,200.00.  Funding to be charged to Operating Budget 
under Curriculum.  Motion passes 9-0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  July 20, 2026 
 
 
2 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the 2026-27 contract with Newsela for Formative 
Digital Platform for the high schools at a cost not to exceed $32,442.65.  Funding to be charged to 
Operating Budget under Curriculum. Motion passes 9-0. 
 
 
• Mosaic Storytelling Program is a platform where teachers, administrators or District office can 
interact and start telling a story of all the great things happening in the classroom. We envision 
anywhere from 80 to 100 stories going out per month that could be shared on our social media 
platform, our website, and really capturing what we're doing. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the Superintendent to enter into a one-year 
agreement with Leaders Atlas to implement the Mosaic Storytelling Program for the 2026–2027 school 
year at a cost not to exceed $18,000.00. Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• Ms. De Gray explains the background of two Special Education RFPs for staffing and support for 
students with high educational needs. 
• Dr. Vicente and Mr. Beer provide details on the contracts with Constellations for McCarthy Middle 
School for the state-approved alternative program serving 15 students.   
• The second contract is for Broad Street and Sunset Heights Elementary Schools for program support 
(serving approximately 70 students in 7 classrooms). 
• The board discusses the importance of keeping students in District and the potential for future 
expansion. 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to award Constellations the Staffing and Management of 
Alternative Program with ABA for the 2026-27 school year at a cost not to exceed $1,150,436.00.  Funding 
to be charged to the Operating Budget under Out-of-District Tuition. Motion passes 8-1 (Ms. Lopez voting 
Nay). 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to award Constellations the Self-Contained ABA Program for 
the 2026-27 school year at a cost not to exceed $2,399,698.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating 
Budget under Contracted Services. Motion passes 9-0. 
 
 
• Ms. Giglio asked for clarification on district-employed or contract-employed psychologists.  Dr. 
Andrade provided clarification. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with White Birch for staffing one 
full-time psychologist for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $162,000.00.  Funding to be 
charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with White Birch for staffing one 
full-time APPIC Fellow and one Doctorate-Level School psychologist for the 2026-2027 school year at a 
cost not to exceed $124,032.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted 
Services.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the three-year contract with Leap Learning for 
staffing one full-time Bilingual psychologist for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed 
$168,750.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  Motion passes 9-
0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  July 20, 2026 
 
 
3 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the contract with Champion Speech Therapy for 
speech services at McCarthy Middle School during the 2026 ESY at a cost not to exceed $14,033.25.  
Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Out-of-District Tuition.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the contract with ABC Physical Therapy for the 
2026-27 school year at a cost not to exceed $270,000.00.  Funding to be charged to account 91.1.022160 
53614.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the contract with Clark Associate for the 2026-27 
school year at a cost not to exceed $976,522.50.  Funding to be charged to account 91.1.022160 53614.  
Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• Ms. De Gray and Dr. Andrade provide the board with details on the request to work with staffing 
agencies to fill 14.5 open special education positions before the school year begins and the next board 
of education meeting on August 24. 
• The board asked clarifying questions about contractors and district-filled positions, the need for staff 
for IEP compliance, and how the Department of Education is helping districts who are finding this 
short-fall in special educators. 
• Dr. Vincente provided clarity around the district’s intent on hiring highly qualified staff to fill these 
roles should the need be. 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to authorize Chief Operating Officer to contract with 
additional qualified staffing agencies, if necessary, after August 1, 2026, to fill remaining special education 
teacher vacancies for 2026-27 school year, with updates on any resulting contracts provided to the BOE.  
Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the FY26 June Transfer Report.  Motion passes 9-
0. 
 
COMMITTEE ON POLICY 
 
• Ms. Raymond reviews the first reading policies and clarifies that EEAA and ECAF should not be on 
first reading as public hearing are required before the board can vote on these policies. 
 
 
COMMITTEE ON HUMAN RESOURCES  
 
• HR committee workshopped the Head Teacher job description.  Additional work will continue until 
next committee meeting. 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the Personnel Recommendations of  
July 20, 2026.    Motion passes 9-0.

NEW BUSINESS 
Communication Plan 
• Dr. Andrade introduces Mr. Dionne, who presents the 2026-2027 communication plan. 
• The plan includes guidelines for email, website, and social media communication, emphasizing 
transparency, consistency, and accessibility. 
• Ms. Raymond raises concerns about legal obligations towards honoring student privacy and the need 
for clear policies on social media usage. 
• Ms. Lewis inquires about the responsibility for managing school social media accounts, specifically 
Instagram. 
• Mr. Dionne explains that he will work with schools over the summer to create individualized 
roadmaps for social media posting.  The approach will depend on the school's community and culture, 
with some schools having multiple administrators posting. 
• Dr. Andrade explains that they are still determining who will be super users and administrators for the 
mosaic hub.  Most administrators will have free access to post, and the system will roll up to Mr. 
Dionne for district-wide dissemination. 
• Ms. Lewis raises concerns about disparities in social media activity between different teams and the 
role of parents in sharing pictures. 
• Dr. Andrade emphasizes the need for consistency in communication and storytelling, regardless of the 
building or team; improving storytelling, and branding across the district, including the BOE. 
• Ms. Bishop suggests researching board-driven social media pages for insights and challenges. 
• The District currently uses Final Site MXRE for District/School to parent communication.  MXRE 
has translation services that supports upwards of 190 languages. 
• Ms. Bishop asks about the use of branded PowerPoint presentations, and Mr. Dionne agrees to work 
on creating consistent templates. 
• Mr. Salvi inquires about phishing email protocols, and Dr. Andrade explains the district's IT filtering 
and phishing exercises. 
• Ms. Lamphier suggests posting the communication progression chart on the website for parental 
reference. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the 2026-27 School Year Communication Plan 
with updates as discussed.  Motion passes 9-0.   
 
 
UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
 
LIAISON REPORTS 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
Alex Homola, 6 Ayer Street, PTO 
• Ms. Homola shares an example of how Mount Pleasant PTO checks social media posts for parental 
rights and McKinney-Vento kids with the Principal. 
BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS 
• Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Lewis, Mr. Salvi, Ms. Lopez, and Ms. Bishop provide brief 
comments and well wishes for the summer. 
• Ms. Heather Raymond reminds the community about free summer lunches and the upcoming Nashua 
Goes Back to School Night. 
• Ms. Bishop discusses the board's presence at the school night event and the need for authorization to 
speak on behalf of the board.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  July 20, 2026 
 
 
6 
• Board members express their appreciation for the work of school staff and provide updates on 
summer programs and resources for students in need. 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to adjourn.  So voted at 7:50 pm.
